sections.name: settings
sections.notes: All active settings emitted by the current Smithproxy saver are administrator-visible, typed, and editable with ranges aligned to the pinned upstream schema. Missing optional settings groups are materialized atomically when their defaults are first changed. Ordered interface-role selectors support complete create, edit, reorder, and delete operations. Non-QUIC worker pools accept non-negative counts and defer the target-specific hardware ceiling to authoritative Smithproxy validation; QUIC accepts -1, 0, or 1. Non-canonical legacy live worker values remain readable without being resubmitted when unrelated settings change. OCSP and CRL cache TTLs are fully editable. Integer quotas accept the full lossless JSON range. HTTP API keys use a masked repeatable editor; allowed management clients, nameservers, and UDP quick ports use explicit value rows with add and remove actions. HTTP API and webhook identities, endpoints, bind targets, administration identity, filesystem paths, credentials, syslog targets, filename components, and rating keys remain visible and reopen from drafts without re-entry. Deprecated thread-spray tuning keys are accepted and ignored by Smithproxy and are intentionally not exposed.

sections.name: debug
sections.notes: Global debug flags and the current per-module boolean, integer, and bounded string logging overrides are typed and editable. Module names are constrained to draft-path-safe identifiers.

sections.name: networking
sections.notes: The complete smithproxy-networkd networking.cfg contract is visible and typed in the GUI. Interception, routing, sysctl, exemption, bypass, restart identity, and tenant-scope fields use drafts aligned to Networkd validation. Interface selectors, tenant ranges, interception ports, and exempt user IDs use explicit value rows instead of comma-authored lists. Every bypass rule requires a concrete destination port from 1 through 65535. Table, control-socket, tenant-index, and tenant-range changes are published atomically but require a controlled Networkd restart; registry validation remains authoritative. Clearing an explicit control-socket override atomically removes the setting and restores Networkd's tenant-derived default. Empty interface selectors are accepted so TPROXY admission can be disabled and its scope cleared atomically. Clearing tenant ranges removes the tenant-0 override and restores Networkd's implicit all-address scope.

sections.name: gui
sections.notes: The persistent gui.cfg schema includes bounded salted scrypt administrator verifiers and an optional absolute frontend asset root. Passwords and enrollment tokens never enter CFtar. Privilege-15 CLI capabilities support initial enrollment, peer creation, and password rotation; published verifiers activate immediately and revoke older sessions for the target identity. Confirmed peer removal protects both the active and final administrator. The frontend override, Smithproxy connection, and browser-gateway groups are independently optional and can be explicitly enabled or removed without silently materializing deployment paths or credentials. The browser validates and publishes configuration in one explicit action only through the authenticated Smithproxy core archive API with running-revision and archive-hash preconditions. CFtar stores boot credential paths, never token or gateway-secret values; those are protected boot-time files. Other boot-setting changes require a controlled restart after publication.

sections.name: address_objects
sections.notes: The pinned Smithproxy schema supports CIDR and FQDN address objects only; both are represented by typed edit and structural create drawers. CIDR inputs show their normalized address range. FQDN inputs require a bounded ASCII DNS host name, reject IP literals before reaching the draft, and provide an explicit best-effort DNS evaluation from the GUI core without contacting the resolved targets or changing the draft. A live object can prefill an explicit copy from its persistent and pending values without baking in temporary augment overlays. Confirmed structural deletion is available only for objects without live or pending policy/routing references and without pending field edits. Visible unused address, port, and protocol objects can be staged for deletion together in one confirmed atomic batch using the same dependency guards. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: port_objects
sections.notes: Port ranges are represented by typed edit and structural create drawers. Creation validates ascending bounded ranges; a live range can prefill an explicit copy from its persistent and pending values without baking in temporary augment overlays. Confirmed deletion is limited to objects without live or pending policy/routing references and without pending field edits. Visible unused address, port, and protocol objects can be staged for deletion together in one confirmed atomic batch using the same dependency guards. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: proto_objects
sections.notes: Protocol identifiers are represented by typed edit and structural create drawers. Creation validates unique protocol numbers in the Smithproxy-supported range 1-255; a live object can prefill an explicit copy but requires a new number before saving and never bakes in temporary augment overlays. Confirmed deletion is limited to objects without live or pending policy references and without pending field edits. Visible unused address, port, and protocol objects can be staged for deletion together in one confirmed atomic batch using the same dependency guards. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: detection_profiles
sections.notes: All active fields emitted by the current detection-profile saver are typed, editable, structurally creatable, and safely duplicable from persistent and pending values without augment overlays. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion individually or through filtered atomic cleanup.

sections.name: captures
sections.notes: All active capture fields are administrator-visible, typed, and editable. Numeric quotas accept the full lossless JSON integer range supported by the GUI transport. Paths, filename components, destination addresses, and interface names reopen from drafts without re-entry. When a legacy or minimal configuration omits local, remote, or options, the v2 transaction creates only the missing parent groups and their complete typed values atomically; older transaction contracts remain read-only for that partial tree.

sections.name: content_profiles
sections.notes: All content-profile fields and nested rule expressions are administrator-visible, typed, editable, structurally creatable, reorderable, and deletable. Draft values are returned in full and reopen without re-entry; expression byte sequences are preserved when an unchanged textarea is saved.

sections.name: tls_ca
sections.notes: Authority names and filesystem paths are fully visible and editable. Authorities support structural creation, duplication, rename, and confirmed deletion; pending paths reopen without re-entry.

sections.name: tls_profiles
sections.notes: All active fields saved by the current Smithproxy TLS profile schema are typed, visible, editable, structurally creatable, and duplicable from persistent and pending values. SNI bypass names and certificate-warning ports use repeatable value editors instead of administrator-authored JSON or comma-separated text and reopen from drafts without re-entry.

sections.name: ssh_profiles
sections.notes: All active SSH profile fields, including host-key paths, are administrator-visible, typed, editable, structurally creatable, and duplicable from persistent and pending values.

sections.name: alg_dns_profiles
sections.notes: The current DNS ALG profile schema is represented by typed edit, complete structural create, and safe persistent-plus-pending duplicate drawers that exclude augment overlays. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion individually or through filtered atomic cleanup.

sections.name: routing
sections.notes: All active fields emitted by the current routing-profile saver are typed, editable, structurally creatable, and safely duplicable from persistent and pending values without augment overlays, with bounded unique destination lists. Create and edit flows use the same object-aware destination picker while retaining explicit literal or unresolved values. Address and port references resolve current draft-visible names while preserving stable live entity IDs. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion individually or through filtered atomic cleanup.

sections.name: policy
sections.notes: All active policy fields returned by the snapshot contract, including ingress and egress interface-role selectors and legacy authentication-profile assignment, are represented by typed edit and ordered structural create drawers. Empty source, source-port, destination, destination-port, ingress-role, egress-role, and profile selectors preserve Smithproxy wildcard or disabled semantics. New action, NAT, and feature writes are constrained to the pinned Smithproxy enums; non-canonical legacy live values remain readable and can be migrated without resubmitting them when another field changes. References resolve live entities by their current draft-visible names and named objects or profiles created earlier in the same workspace draft; pending creates reopen their structural drawer and pending renames retain the stable live entity ID. Ordered creates and moves may target earlier pending policies through transaction-scoped client identifiers while use-before-create choices remain unavailable. Existing policies support optimistic first, before, and last move operations; restoring the original position removes the pending move. Selected live policies can move first or last in one atomic batch while preserving their internal order and avoiding no-op drafts. Confirmed single or selected-policy structural deletion is staged atomically and rejects conflicting pending field edits, structural operations, and removal of a position anchor used by another pending policy. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: starttls_signatures
sections.notes: All signature metadata, matcher expressions, and ordered flow controls are administrator-visible and typed. Parents and flow steps support structural creation, editing, ordering, and deletion; complete draft expressions reopen without re-entry and preserve unchanged byte sequences.

sections.name: detection_signatures
sections.notes: All signature metadata, matcher expressions, and ordered flow controls are administrator-visible and typed. Parents and flow steps support structural creation, editing, ordering, and deletion; complete draft expressions reopen without re-entry and preserve unchanged byte sequences.

sections.name: script_profiles
sections.notes: All active script-profile fields, including executable module paths, are administrator-visible, typed, editable, structurally creatable, and duplicable from persistent and pending values.

sections.name: auth_profiles
sections.notes: Legacy authentication profiles remain fully visible and editable for complete configuration administration. Profile flags and complete identity mappings support typed draft editing even though new deployments should avoid this obsolete runtime mechanism.
